## Introduction

This post provides the code to set up and estimate a basic Bayesian vector error correction (BVEC) model with the `bvartools` package. The presented Gibbs sampler is based on the approach of Koop et al. (2010), who propose a prior on the cointegration space.

## Data

To illustrate the estimation process, the dataset E6 from Lütkepohl (2007) is used, which contains data on German long-term interest rates and inflation from 1972Q2 to 1998Q4.

```{r data, message=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=4.5}
library("bvartools")

data("e6")

plot(e6) # Plot the series
```

The `create_bvecmodel` function produces an object of class `bvecmodel`, whose element `data$train` contains the inputs `y`, `w` and `x` for the BVEC estimator, where `y` is the matrix of dependent variables, `w` is a matrix of potentially cointegrated regressors, and `x` is the matrix of non-cointegration regressors. The matrices contain one row per period. Since the sampler below is written for matrices with one column per period, they are transposed.

```{r}
model <- create_bvecmodel(e6,
                          p = 4,
                          r = 1,
                          const = "unrestricted",
                          seasonal = "unrestricted")

y <- t(model[["data"]][["train"]][["y"]])
w <- t(model[["data"]][["train"]][["w"]])
x <- t(model[["data"]][["train"]][["x"]])
```

## Estimation

```{r flat prior}
# Reset random number generator for reproducibility
set.seed(7654321)

iter <- 10000 # Number of iterations of the Gibbs sampler
burnin <- 5000 # Number of burn-in draws
store <- iter - burnin

r <- 1 # Set rank

tt <- ncol(y) # Number of observations
k <- nrow(y) # Number of endogenous variables
k_w <- nrow(w) # Number of regressors in error correction term
# Number of differenced regressors and unrestricted deterministic terms
k_x <- nrow(x)

k_alpha <- k * r # Number of elements in alpha
k_beta <- k_w * r # Number of elements in beta
k_gamma <- k * k_x

# Set uninformative priors
# ...for loadings and non-cointegration parameters
# Vector of prior parameter means
a_mu_prior <- matrix(0, k_alpha + k_gamma)
# Inverse of the prior covariance matrix
a_v_i_prior <- diag(0, k_alpha + k_gamma)

# ...for cointegration parameters
v_i <- 0
p_tau_i <- matrix(0, k_w, k_w)
p_tau_i[1:r, 1:r] <- diag(1, r)

#...for the error term
u_sigma_df_prior <- r # Prior degrees of freedom
u_sigma_scale_prior <- diag(0, k) # Prior covariance matrix
u_sigma_df_post <- tt + u_sigma_df_prior # Posterior degrees of freedom

# Initial values
beta_draw <- matrix(c(1, -4), k_w, r)

u_sigma_i <- diag(.0001, k)
u_sigma <- solve(u_sigma_i)

g_i <- u_sigma_i

# Data containers
draws_alpha <- matrix(NA, k_alpha, store)
draws_beta <- matrix(NA, k_beta, store)
draws_pi <- matrix(NA, k * k_w, store)
draws_gamma <- matrix(NA, k_gamma, store)
draws_sigma <- matrix(NA, k^2, store)

# Start Gibbs sampler
for (draw in 1:iter) {
  # Draw conditional mean parameters
  temp <- post_coint_kls(y = y,
                         beta = beta_draw,
                         w = w,
                         x = x,
                         sigma_i = u_sigma_i,
                         v_i = v_i,
                         p_tau_i = p_tau_i,
                         g_i = g_i,
                         gamma_mu_prior = a_mu_prior,
                         gamma_v_i_prior = a_v_i_prior)
  alpha_draw <- temp[["alpha"]]
  beta_draw <- temp[["beta"]]
  pi_draw <- temp[["Pi"]]
  gamma_draw <- temp[["Gamma"]]

  # Draw variance-covariance matrix
  u <- y - pi_draw %*% w - matrix(gamma_draw, k) %*% x
  beta_p_beta <- crossprod(beta_draw, p_tau_i) %*% beta_draw
  alpha_prior <- v_i * alpha_draw %*% tcrossprod(beta_p_beta, alpha_draw)
  u_sigma_scale_post <- solve(tcrossprod(u) + alpha_prior)
  u_sigma_i <- rWishart(1, u_sigma_df_post, u_sigma_scale_post)[, , 1]
  u_sigma_i <- matrix(u_sigma_i, k)
  u_sigma <- solve(u_sigma_i)

  # Update g_i
  g_i <- u_sigma_i

  # Store draws
  if (draw > burnin) {
    draws_alpha[, draw - burnin] <- alpha_draw
    draws_beta[, draw - burnin] <- beta_draw
    draws_pi[, draw - burnin] <- pi_draw
    draws_gamma[, draw - burnin] <- gamma_draw
    draws_sigma[, draw - burnin] <- u_sigma
  }
}
```

Obtain point estimates as the mean of the parameter draws:

```{r}
gamma_mean <- rowMeans(draws_gamma) # Obtain means for every row
gamma_mean <- matrix(gamma_mean, k) # Transform mean vector into a matrix
gamma_mean <- round(gamma_mean, 3) # Round values
# Rename matrix dimensions
dimnames(gamma_mean) <- list(dimnames(y)[[1]], dimnames(x)[[1]])

round(gamma_mean, 3) # Print
```

```{r beta}
# Obtain means for every row
beta_mean <- rowMeans(t(t(draws_beta) / t(draws_beta)[, 1]))
beta_mean <- matrix(beta_mean, k_w) # Transform mean vector into a matrix
beta_mean <- round(beta_mean, 3) # Round values
dimnames(beta_mean) <- list(dimnames(w)[[1]], NULL) # Rename matrix dimensions

beta_mean # Print
```

```{r}
sigma_mean <- rowMeans(draws_sigma) # Obtain means for every row
sigma_mean <- matrix(sigma_mean, k) # Transform mean vector into a matrix
sigma_mean <- round(sigma_mean * 10^4, 2) # Round values
# Rename matrix dimensions
dimnames(sigma_mean) <- list(dimnames(y)[[1]], dimnames(y)[[1]])

sigma_mean # Print
```

## `bvec` objects

The `bvec` function can be used to collect output of the Gibbs sampler in a standardised object, which can be used further for forecasting, impulse response analysis or forecast error variance decomposition.

```{r bvec-object}
# Number of non-deterministic coefficients
k_nondet <- (k_x - 4) * k

# Generate bvec object
bvec_est <- bvec(y = model[["data"]][["train"]][["y"]],
                 w = model[["data"]][["train"]][["w"]],
                 x = model[["data"]][["train"]][["x"]][, 1:6],
                 x_d = model[["data"]][["train"]][["x"]][, 7:10],
                 r = 1,
                 alpha = draws_alpha,
                 beta = draws_beta,
                 Gamma = draws_gamma[1:k_nondet, ],
                 C = draws_gamma[(k_nondet + 1):nrow(draws_gamma), ],
                 Sigma = draws_sigma)
```

The error correction term is described by the draws of `alpha` and `beta` and not by those of `Pi`, since the latter cannot be decomposed into the former.

Posterior draws can be thinned with function `thin`:

```{r thin}
bvec_est <- thin(bvec_est, thin = 5)
```

The function `vec_to_var` can be used to transform the VEC model into a VAR in levels:

```{r vec2var}
bvar_form <- vec_to_var(bvec_est)
```

## Forecasts

Forecasts are obtained in two steps. First, function `add_forecast_input` generates the data of the forecast periods. Values of deterministic terms such as the seasonal dummies can be provided in its argument `deterministic`. If they are not provided, the function tries to obtain them from the model. Second, function `add_posterior_forecasts` simulates the forecasts.

```{r forecast, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=4}
bvar_form <- add_forecast_input(bvar_form, n_ahead = 10)
bvar_form <- add_posterior_forecasts(bvar_form)

bvar_pred <- predict(bvar_form, n_ahead = 10)

plot(bvar_pred, n_pre = 20)
```

## Impulse response analysis

Impulse responses for VECs can be constructed from their VAR respresentations.

```{r feir, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=4.5}
ir <- irf(bvar_form, impulse = "R", response = "Dp", n_ahead = 20)

plot(ir,
     main = "Forecast Error Impulse Response",
     xlab = "Year",
     ylab = "Response")
```

### Orthogonalised impulse response

```{r oir, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=4.5}
oir <- irf(bvar_form,
           impulse = "R",
           response = "Dp",
           n_ahead = 20,
           type = "oir")

plot(oir,
     main = "Orthogonalised Impulse Response",
     xlab = "Year",
     ylab = "Response")
```

### Generalised impulse response

```{r gir, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=4.5}
gir <- irf(bvar_form,
           impulse = "R",
           response = "Dp",
           n_ahead = 20,
           type = "gir")

plot(gir,
     main = "Generalised Impulse Response",
     xlab = "Year",
     ylab = "Response")
```

### Forecast error variance decomposition

```{r fevd, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=4.5}
bvec_fevd <- fevd(bvar_form, response = "Dp", n_ahead = 20)

plot(bvec_fevd, main = "FEVD of inflation")
```
